title: Add & subtract fractions
examples: Teacher, what do I do if the denominators are different?
Can you show me another example of simplifying?
Do I always need to find the least common multiple?

explain.say: Today we learn to add and subtract fractions. Sometimes the bottom numbers are different. We must make them the same first.

items: Must make them the same first

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: fractions of a pie. Look at the whole pie, the one slice and the three eighths. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

If the bottom numbers are different, we need a common denominator. This is the smallest number both can divide into. We call this the least common denominator. For example, find the LCD of two and three.

To change the fractions, we multiply the top and the bottom by the same number. For example, to change one over two, we multiply top and bottom by three. This gives us three over six. Then we can add the tops. One plus three equals four. So we get four over six.

After adding or subtracting, we must simplify the answer. Simplifying means making the fraction smaller. We divide the top and the bottom by the same number. For example, six over six simplifies to one over one. Wait, six over six is just one.

faq.q: What if the denominators are already the same?
faq.a: If the bottom numbers are the same, you just add or subtract the top numbers. You keep the bottom number the same. For example, three over eight plus two over eight is five over eight.
asks: Do I do anything if the bottoms match?
What if the denominators are equal?

faq.q: Why do I have to find the least common denominator?
faq.a: We find the LCD so that the pieces we are counting are the same size. You cannot add apples and oranges unless you count them both as fruit. The LCD makes the pieces the same size.
asks: Why is the LCD important for adding?
Must I always use the least common multiple?

faq.a: Simplifying means finding the biggest number that divides both the top and the bottom evenly. You divide both numbers by that biggest number. For example, twelve over eighteen can be divided by three to get four over six. Wait, twelve over eighteen can be divided by three to get four over six. Wait, twelve over eighteen can be divided by six to get two over three.
asks: How do I make a fraction smaller?
What is the easiest way to simplify?

faq.q: Can I use any common denominator?
faq.a: Yes, you can use any common denominator. However, using the least common denominator keeps the numbers smaller and easier to work with. It is the best practice.
asks: Is there a rule for the common denominator?
Does it matter which common denominator I pick?

faq.q: What if I subtract and the top becomes negative?
faq.a: If the top number becomes negative, the answer is a negative fraction. You keep the negative sign on the top number. For example, two over three minus five over three is negative three over three.
asks: How do I handle subtraction that goes below zero?

facts: To add or subtract fractions, denominators must match.
The least common denominator is the smallest number divisible by all given denominators.
To change a fraction, multiply the top and bottom by the same whole number.
Simplifying means dividing the numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor.

quiz.say: Calculate and simplify: one over two plus one over three.
quiz.why: The LCD of two and three is six. One over two becomes three over six. One over three becomes two over six. Three plus two is five, so the answer is five over six.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you try to add the numerators and denominators without finding a common base.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you incorrectly add the numerators and denominators together.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you only change one of the fractions and forget the other one.

quiz.say: Calculate and simplify: three over four minus one over eight.
quiz.why: The LCD of four and eight is eight. Three over four becomes six over eight. Six minus one is five, so the answer is five over eight.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you only subtract the numerators and keep the original denominator.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you forget to change the three over four into eighths.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you do not correctly find the common denominator before subtracting.

quiz.say: What is the simplest form of twelve over eighteen?
quiz.why: The greatest common divisor of twelve and eighteen is six. Dividing both twelve and eighteen by six gives two over three.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you only divide by two, which is a common factor but not the greatest one.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you forget to simplify the fraction at all.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you only divide the top and bottom by two, but then forget to simplify again.
